Under the identification assumptions
([Consistency](causal-inference.qmd#def-consistency),
[Conditional Exchangeability](causal-inference.qmd#def-exchangeability),
and [Positivity](causal-inference.qmd#def-positivity)),
we estimate that Type A behavioral pattern
causally increases CHD risk by
`r round(marginal_rd_est * 100, 2)` percentage points
compared to Type B behavioral pattern,
after standardizing over the observed age distribution
(95% CI:
`r round(ci_lower * 100, 2)` to
`r round(ci_upper * 100, 2)` percentage points).

Because this rendered example uses `r B` [bootstrap samples](https://morrison-lab.github.io/sds/bootstrap.html#def-bootstrap-sample),
the displayed [standard error](https://morrison-lab.github.io/sds/estimation.html#def-SE) and [confidence interval](https://morrison-lab.github.io/sds/inference.html#def-confidence-interval) are illustrative.
For final inferential reporting,
rerun with at least 2000 bootstrap samples.

A 95% CI that excludes zero does not by itself imply
practical or clinical importance;
also interpret the estimated [risk difference](binary-outcome-associations.qmd#def-RD) magnitude.
